correctness.rationale: Use local odd map F_h(x)=x−hK_N sin x near the phase-opposition fixed point. K_N has simple top eigenvalue λ_N=2+2cos(π/(N+1)); the other linear eigenvalues stay strictly inside the unit circle when h crosses 2/λ_N. The mean equation of a nearby 2-cycle has invertible derivative DF−I=−hK_N; oddness forces its centre to zero. Thus 2x=hK_N sin x. Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction onto the top eigenvector gives reduced equation s[−λ_Nδ+(S_N/3)s²+O(δs²+s⁴)]=0, with S_N>0, yielding exactly the two opposite points for δ>0 and none for δ≤0. The Jacobian at either point is I−hK_N diag(cos x_i) similar to a real symmetric matrix near the branch; its critical multiplier −1+2λ_Nδ+O(δ²) squares to 1−4λ_Nδ+O(δ²), others remain strictly stable. Explicit S_N=3/(2(N+1)) for N≥2 and S_1=1 handle the boundary. The imported strict Lyapunov descent below threshold is stated separately. Independent roots and Jacobian eigenvalues checked 10 parameter cases without substituting for the all-N proof.

value.rationale: The critical bifurcation is a natural question explicitly left by the strict-descent stability threshold in a discrete physical oscillator network. Exact all-path amplitude, spatial sine-eigenmode and local Floquet stability distinguish a merely lost Lyapunov inequality from an actually created attracting recurrent oscillation.

final_claim: For every fixed N≥1 and h immediately above 2/λ_N, the torus path map z↦z+hK_N sin z acquires exactly one locally unique attracting prime 2-cycle near phase opposition, asymptotically ±sqrt(3λ_N(h−2/λ_N)/S_N)v with critical Floquet multiplier 1−4λ_N(h−2/λ_N)+O((h−2/λ_N)^2).
limitations: Small positive h−h_N only; neighborhood and parameter width may depend on N.
Global orbits at larger coupling and unreduced neutral global phase are outside scope.
